Is there a preferred rollback policy for canary rollouts during EU activation?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Caroline Ng, Diego Morales, Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Nina Patel, Omar Reyes, Sofia Ivanova, Marcus Lee (AtlasFold)

[00:00] Caroline: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:06] Nina: Yep good, thanks.
[00:09] Caroline: Cool, agenda: renewal confirmation, the staggered top-up across EU regions, KMS details for private onramp, and quick perf validation Diego mentioned. Priya will recap support / billing bits at the end.
[00:22] Marcus: Sounds good. We only have 45 minutes so maybe focus on the blockers, yeah?
[00:28] Diego: Perfect. I'll try to keep the deep tech to the end so legal can leave if needed.

--- Discovery / context (rough) ---
[00:35] Nina: To recap our side — AtlasFold is at about 12M tokens/day on average, spikes to 45M with seasonality. We're seeing P95 around 420ms on current US region, P99 is 1.1s. Our ask: keep latency below 500ms P95 post-EU onramp and avoid a big billing delta.
[00:58] Omar: Also we need data residency guarantees for EU customer set by Q4; that's non-negotiable.
[01:05] Caroline: Understood. For residency we can do a Private onramp into EU region with VPC and KMS. That would pin data to EU nodes; Diego can walk through what that looks like.
[01:14] Diego: Quick note — our Dedicated pools can be provisioned in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1, we typically recommend eu-central for lower egress to EU partners; the uplift time for a reserved Dedicated cluster is about 7-10 business days after order, shorter with pre-warm.
[01:30] Omar: 7-10 business days is fine if we sign off soon. Can we get predictable throughput? We need to test with our reranking workload which has short sequences but high concurrency.
[01:41] Diego: Yep the plan is to configure continuous batching and per-route concurrency limits; for reranking we suggest a smaller seq-opt model variant and a higher qps pool. We'll validate on your test harness.

--- Contract and pricing ---
[01:55] Liam: From billing — current committed level ends 2025-09-30. AtlasFold asked for a staged top-up: +30% in month 1, +20% in month 3, +50% month 6 (cumulative). We can do a contract amendment with staggered billing and a blended rate for the top-up period.
[02:12] Sofia: Legal here — we need the precise amendment language, specifically the failover SLA and liability cap during cross-region failover.
[02:19] Caroline: We'll propose sample SLA wording; our default is 99.9% for Dedicated with a cross-region fallback trigger. We can add a clause for automatic reroute and a 30-day notice window for region maintenance.
[02:32] Marcus: Is there a charge for automatic failover usage?
[02:35] Liam: Failover usage is billed at the same unit rate but we can add a 60% credit for the first 48 hours of emergency cross-region use in the first 90 days to ease the ramp.

--- Technical deep dive (SE-led) ---
[02:50] Diego: I'll sketch the plan: 1) Run a ~2hr perf baseline against your rerank+generate mix in our staging Dedicated; 2) Validate P95/P99 and token CPU; 3) Test KMS integration (we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys via import to our HSM) but note we had a couple of customers call it out as K-M-S import got sticky — sometimes metadata wasn't preserved in the first run.
[03:13] Nina: Hmm, can you confirm we can bring our own keys and that key rotation is on our schedule?
[03:20] Diego: Yes BYOK supported, rotation can be scheduled; we have HSM-backed key wrapping. There is a short integration step where the infra team needs to confirm the policies.
[03:28] Omar: On the KV cache — internal name sometimes comes across as "K-V cash" in older transcripts — just to be explicit, we need sticky prefix caching between EU and US during gradual rollouts so tokens don't get re-generated.
[03:39] Diego: Right — cross-region prefix caching won't happen natively; we do prefix caching per-cluster. During rollouts we either warm caches via synthetic pre-seeding or route stickily by user-id to EU cluster once warm. We'll show tradeoffs in the perf run.

--- Risks and tradeoffs ---
[03:55] Nina: Main concern: cost blowout during spike in month 2 while EU is still warming. How do we mitigate?
[04:04] Liam: Two levers — 1) A temporary burst pool with capped burst hours and 2) request-level throttling to preserve SLOs (we prioritize low-latency routes). We'll include an allowance in the amendment for 120 burst hours over 90 days.
[04:18] Marcus: What about model quantization? Could we reduce cost without altering outputs?
[04:22] Diego: For reranking we can run a quantized candidate model for scoring and full-precision for the top candidate; it's a classic cost/latency trade. We'll include recommended quantization profiles in the perf readout.

--- Operational / Security ---
[04:40] Priya: On support: you'll keep CSM triage + 24/7 oncall for Dedicated critical incidents. We'll set up an escalation matrix. For audit logs, we can retain 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on.
[04:52] Sofia: SOC 2 and ISO docs? We need the latest reports and any third-party pen test summaries.
[04:57] Caroline: I'll attach the SOC2 Type II and ISO certs. The pen-test summary is in the security pack; Diego will also flag the KMS import caveat.

--- Recap & Next steps ---
[05:10] Caroline: Quick recap: AtlasFold will proceed with renewal at base commit; contract amendment to add staged top-up and EU Dedicated activation. Action items as listed — Caroline to send pricing + draft amendment by Friday, Diego to run perf baseline and share results, Omar to send traffic distribution, Sofia to review legal language. Priya to set up kickoff for VPC/KMS once amendment signed.
[05:35] Nina: That matches. One ask — can we do a quick smoke test inside EU with a small pre-warm before the full top-up?
[05:42] Diego: Yes we can do a 24-48hr pre-warm and smoke run; we'll include that in the test plan.
[05:47] Sofia: Also want to see a sample run-book for rollbacks.
[05:50] Priya: We'll share the rollback run-book and can align on on-call contacts.
[05:55] Caroline: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up with the doc links and pricing spreadsheet.
[06:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some names mis-transcribed in places, acronyms occasionally expanded (K-M-S), timestamps approximate.
